speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider sending a letter in the four official languages to all seniors aged 60 years and above to encourage them to make a Lasting Power of Attorney and also to inform them the steps they need to take to make one.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current number of Singaporeans who have registered a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) since the establishment of the Office of the Public Guardian; (b) whether there are plans to assist more Singaporeans to register for a LPA through the new digital process, especially the seniors; and (c) whether there can be more non-digital ways made available to help seniors sign up.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I would invite Members to seek clarifications, if need be.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If the questions have been addressed, it may not be necessary for them to proceed with the questions for future Sittings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have stepped up efforts to increase awareness and take up of Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPA) over the years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have seen a significant increase in LPA registrations since its introduction.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In 2013, around 2,200 Singaporeans registered an LPA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In designing the e-service, we paid extra attention to seniors and those less comfortable with technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, the application form will be an easy questionnaire that guides the user in creating his or her LPA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Instructions are in plain English and are also available in the other official languages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Additionally, users can view step-by-step instructional videos in the four official languages and Quick Reference Guides to help them navigate the e-service.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have tested the service with older users, who reported they were confident to use it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Office of the Public Guardian is also working with partners to provide help at convenient locations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Residents who prefer in-person assistance can approach ServiceSG Centres, Citizen Connect Centres and the Office of the Public Guardian.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Officers there will be able to help them with the online LPA application.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Staff at other community touchpoints – such as Senior Activity Centres, restructured hospitals and nursing homes – will also be able to provide advice to residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are happy to work with Members to promote this to their residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will consider how a letter-mailing exercise can be carried out in a cost-effective way, perhaps riding on other regular mail correspondence that the Government already sends to residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Family members will also be vital channels of outreach.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Whether as a spouse, child or grandchild, we should encourage our loved ones to make their LPAs early, so that they are better prepared should they lose their mental capacity one day.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Single and lonely elderly sometimes find it very difficult to identify suitable donees.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can MSF help our elderly by matching them with perhaps a pre-screened list of potential donees?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If there is not such a list of persons, can MSF maybe consider doing so?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will study this suggestion and we welcome other suggestions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As we operate the OPGO from the middle of November, we will have to study how the public reacts to it, especially our seniors, and then accommodate, adjust, so that as many of them as possible will be enrolled in the LPA.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One is, does the Ministry track the adoption of LPA, those who apply, by age group above 60, maybe in 10-year bands?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because I think the older they are the more this is important for them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very heartened to hear the high absolute number growth, but I am not sure what it is from the baseline.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, do we track the percentage of our population above 60 years old by 10-year bands on their adoption of LPA?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second question is, for those that may have more difficulties getting an LPA, will the Ministry consider an opt-out scheme where appropriate donees are given to them and if they opt out, then they cannot be a part of LPA?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For internal, specific purposes, we do track who are on, who have been enrolled, so that we can see by trend, at what age they enrol.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think it is noteworthy that while we want those who are above 50 as our target to be on LPA, I think all of us should be on LPA as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And even for our children to be on LPA and not think that it is something we can postpone until usually too late.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the other question, it is the same as what Ms Joan Pereira has asked.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will study all the suggestions that Members have and, of course, the experience we have on the ground, incorporate them, adjust our process and procedures as we move.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: That has been the trend for the past few years of several rounds of extension of the waiver.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I wish to understand whether the Ministry intends to consider extending the waiver indefinitely.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second question is in relation to stepping up on the outreach.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Silver Generation Ambassadors have been a good touchpoint in interacting with our seniors.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, whether OPG intends to train our Silver Generation Ambassadors, so that as part of the outreach, one of the key topics that the Ambassadors can consider to do, is to broach this topic in relation to the importance of doing an LPA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I do not think, though, that the fee is the only reason why people do not take up an LPA.
